cases.name: The Missing Blackwood Ledger
cases.premise: The 1823 town ledger, which says who really owns half of Hollow Creek, has vanished from the Library.
cases.recovered: The ledger is back in the Library, and Hollow Creek finally knows who owns what.

suspects.name: Gus Thornbury
suspects.bio: Has tended the Blackwood grounds for forty years and hates visitors trampling his roses.
suspects.alibi: Says he was locking up the Greenhouse all evening.
suspects.motive: to keep the ledger from showing the greenhouse land was never his family's

suspects.name: Vivian Blackwood
suspects.bio: Inherits the manor next month, unless it's 'too haunted' to sell.
suspects.alibi: Claims she was in the Library reading all night.
suspects.motive: to tear out the page that splits her inheritance with a long-lost cousin

suspects.name: Reginald Pike
suspects.bio: Has been trying to buy the manor's antiques for a song.
suspects.alibi: Insists he left before sunset and spent the evening at the Diner in town.
suspects.motive: to sell the ledger to a collector in the city while everyone hid from the ghost

suspects.name: Martha Bunce
suspects.bio: Bakes the best pies in the county and knows every servants' passage.
suspects.alibi: Says she was in the Kitchen baking for tomorrow's party until midnight.
suspects.motive: to hide the old recipe pages tucked inside it, the ones her prize pies are copied from

clues.name: Muddy boot print
clues.description: Fresh garden mud, heavy work boots.

clues.name: Whiff of lavender
clues.description: Expensive lavender perfume lingers on the curtain.

clues.name: Cigar ash
clues.description: Still-warm ash from an imported cigar.

clues.name: Floury handprint
clues.description: A perfect handprint in baking flour.

clues.name: Dropped key ring
clues.description: A ring of old master keys to the manor.

clues.name: Fresh rose petals
clues.description: Petals from the manor's prize rose garden.

clues.name: Loose pearl
clues.description: A real pearl from a broken necklace.

clues.name: Torn leather glove
clues.description: A fine leather glove, torn on a nail.

cases.name: The Missing Harvest Lantern
cases.premise: The Harvest Lantern that leads the festival's lantern walk has vanished from Mrs. Pemberton's mantel, and her teapot hasn't stopped rattling since.
cases.recovered: The Harvest Lantern is back on Mrs. Pemberton's mantel, just in time for the lantern walk.

suspects.name: Hank Moody
suspects.bio: Has been 'fixing' Mrs. Pemberton's shed since June and charges by the hour.
suspects.alibi: Says he was fixing the lock on the Garden Shed, then went home with a sore back.
suspects.motive: to sell the lantern's old brass to a scrap dealer and blame it on the ghost

suspects.name: Daisy Pemberton
suspects.bio: Wants the cottage for herself, and Grandma won't move out while the teapot behaves.
suspects.alibi: Claims she was at the Diner in town with friends all evening.
suspects.motive: to scare Grandma into moving out, lantern and all

suspects.name: Leonard Crisp
suspects.bio: Already has a buyer lined up for a 'charming, slightly haunted' cottage.
suspects.alibi: Insists he was showing a house on Elm Street.
suspects.motive: to pocket the lantern and sell his buyer a 'charmingly haunted' cottage

suspects.name: Beatrice Hollis
suspects.bio: Runs the bake-off club and has wanted that prize-winning garden for years.
suspects.alibi: Says she was icing cupcakes in Mrs. Pemberton's Kitchen, as a favour.
suspects.motive: to carry the lantern in the walk herself and finally win the garden prize

clues.name: Pile of sawdust
clues.description: Fresh sawdust, the kind you get from sawing a shed door.

clues.name: Pink glitter
clues.description: Party glitter, still sparkling on the windowsill.

clues.name: Greasy smudge
clues.description: A hair-pomade smudge on the hall mirror. Smells of limes.

clues.name: Icing sugar
clues.description: A dusting of icing sugar on the doorknob.

clues.name: Spare key
clues.description: The spare key from under the flowerpot, left on the rug.

clues.name: Potting soil
clues.description: Rich potting soil from the vegetable patch, trodden indoors.

clues.name: Gold locket
clues.description: A gold locket with a tiny photo of the cottage inside.

clues.name: Spilled tea leaves
clues.description: Chamomile tea leaves, scattered as if the pot leapt by itself.

cases.name: The Sabotaged Prize Display
cases.premise: Someone wrecked the farm's prize pumpkin display the night before judging, and the scarecrow keeps moving.
cases.recovered: The prize display is mended and the judges can come in the morning.

suspects.name: Abel Hatcher
suspects.bio: Runs the farm with his sister and swears the scarecrow moved on its own.
suspects.alibi: Says he was mending the Windmill until it got dark.
suspects.motive: to hide that the prize pumpkin was bought in town, not grown

suspects.name: Clementine Hatcher
suspects.bio: Won the county fair three years running and wants to sell the farm and move to the city.
suspects.alibi: Claims she was rehearsing her parade wave in the Parlor.
suspects.motive: to make the farm lose, so it sells and she can leave for the city

suspects.name: Silas Crane
suspects.bio: Wants to turn the corn maze into a car park, if only the farm were 'too spooky' to keep.
suspects.alibi: Insists he was at the Post Office in town, mailing plans to the county.
suspects.motive: to scare the Hatchers into selling the corn maze for his car park

suspects.name: Ma Jessup
suspects.bio: Sells pies at the farm gate and hears every bit of gossip in the county.
suspects.alibi: Says she was baking apple pies in the Farm Kitchen for the Harvest Festival.
suspects.motive: to make sure her own pie stand takes best in show

clues.name: Hay seeds
clues.description: Seeds from the very top of the hayloft, stuck in a boot tread.

clues.name: Gold glitter
clues.description: Gold pageant glitter on the ladder rungs.

clues.name: Surveyor's chalk
clues.description: Bright blue chalk, the kind used to mark out building plots.

clues.name: Apple peel
clues.description: A long curl of apple peel, still fresh.

clues.name: Barn key
clues.description: The big iron key to the barn, dropped in the straw.

clues.name: Corn husks
clues.description: Husks from the maze, tucked into a pocket and dropped.

clues.name: Rodeo belt buckle
clues.description: A shiny silver buckle shaped like a horseshoe.

clues.name: Tractor grease
clues.description: Black grease on the hayloft hatch. Someone's been near an engine.

cases.name: The Interrupted Recital
cases.premise: The nursery music box keeps cutting off Lavinia's charity recital, and the donation tin went missing in the fuss.
cases.recovered: The donation tin is found and Lavinia's recital goes on, music box and all.

suspects.name: Ezra Cole
suspects.bio: Has kept the Ashcombe garden and family plot tidy since he was a boy.
suspects.alibi: Says he was raking leaves in the Family Plot until the candles burned down.
suspects.motive: to hide that he'd borrowed from the donation tin to mend the family plot gate

suspects.name: Lavinia Ashcombe
suspects.bio: Lives alone in the big house and hasn't slept since the music box started playing.
suspects.alibi: Claims she was locked in the Master Bedroom with the radio on.
suspects.motive: to stop the recital before anyone counted the donation tin

suspects.name: Dr. Felix Marlowe
suspects.bio: Has offered three times to buy the nursery's music box. Three times he was refused.
suspects.alibi: Insists he was at the Bookshop in town until closing.
suspects.motive: to frighten Lavinia into finally selling him the music box

suspects.name: Agnes Pratt
suspects.bio: Knows every creaky floorboard and every secret door in the house.
suspects.alibi: Says she was polishing the silver in the Dining Room for Sunday.
suspects.motive: to slip the donation tin away while everyone stared at the music box

clues.name: Hedge clippings
clues.description: Fresh clippings from the front hedge, tracked up the stairs.

clues.name: Scent of violets
clues.description: Violet perfume, faint but unmistakable, in the nursery.

clues.name: Pipe tobacco
clues.description: A pinch of cherry pipe tobacco on the windowsill.

clues.name: Silver polish
clues.description: A smear of silver polish on the music box's key.

clues.name: Skeleton key
clues.description: An old skeleton key that opens the nursery door.

clues.name: Graveyard dirt
clues.description: Dark soil from the family plot, still damp.

clues.name: Velvet thread
clues.description: A thread of plum velvet caught on the trapdoor.

clues.name: Candle wax
clues.description: Drips of black candle wax leading to the tower stairs.

cases.name: The Mask Keeper
cases.premise: Someone at the Historical Society has been lending out the town's folklore masks, and tonight the oldest of them all, the Hollow Creek Mask, is missing from its case.
cases.recovered: The Hollow Creek Mask is back in its case with the other four, and the museum stays open.

suspects.name: Walter Finch
suspects.bio: Has guarded the museum for thirty years and knows every creaky board and every key.
suspects.alibi: Says he was doing his rounds in the Archive all night.
suspects.motive: so the town would believe in the old legends again, and the museum he has guarded for thirty years would stay open

suspects.name: Edie Wren
suspects.bio: Runs the museum on a shoestring and gives out full-size candy bars. Her fingers are always inky.
suspects.alibi: Claims she was cataloguing in the Reading Room until late.
suspects.motive: to bring the crowds back before the museum closed for good, one haunting at a time

suspects.name: Mortimer Vane
suspects.bio: Keeps the books, and keeps telling the board the building should be sold.
suspects.alibi: Insists he left the board meeting and spent the evening at the Diner.
suspects.motive: to frighten the board into selling the building, masks and all, to his collector friend in the city

suspects.name: Rosa Delgado
suspects.bio: Bakes for every fundraiser and runs the museum's little tea corner in the Gift Shop.
suspects.alibi: Says she was in the Gift Shop pricing raffle prizes.
suspects.motive: to make the Halloween fundraiser the busiest night her little tea room had ever seen

clues.name: Ring of brass keys
clues.description: The watchman's keys, every door in the building, dropped in a hurry.

clues.name: Inky fingerprint
clues.description: A fresh, inky fingerprint on the glass of the mask case.

clues.name: Torn ledger page
clues.description: A page from the society's accounts, columns of sums circled in red.

clues.name: Cake crumbs
clues.description: Crumbs of lemon drizzle cake, all the way along the gallery rope.

clues.name: Old paper dust
clues.description: Grey dust from very old paper, the kind that lives in the archive and the reading room.

clues.name: Lantern oil
clues.description: A drip of lantern oil, from the kind of lamp you carry on rounds or into a cold storeroom.

clues.name: Fountain pen nib
clues.description: A gold fountain pen nib, snapped off. Only a few people here still write with one.

clues.name: Raffle tickets
clues.description: A strip of raffle tickets from the Halloween fundraiser, numbers 101 to 110.

cases.name: The Lost Love Letters
cases.premise: A bundle of letters from the late Mr. Pemberton has vanished from the Study desk, and every night since, the garden gnomes have turned to face the window.
cases.recovered: The letters are back in the Study desk, blue ribbon and all, and Mrs. Pemberton reads one aloud to the club.

suspects.name: Hank Moody
suspects.bio: Back to fix the shed roof he 'definitely' fixed last time. Owes money all over town.
suspects.alibi: Says he was clearing leaves in the Back Garden until dark.
suspects.motive: to hide that the letters mention the money Mr. Pemberton lent him and never got back

suspects.name: Daisy Pemberton
suspects.bio: Staying the week to help Grandma, and asking a lot of questions about the old days.
suspects.alibi: Claims she was at the Bookshop in town choosing a birthday present.
suspects.motive: to read what Grandma never told anyone about where the family's money went

suspects.name: Leonard Crisp
suspects.bio: Has a buyer lined up for the cottage the moment Mrs. Pemberton says yes.
suspects.alibi: Insists he was at the Post Office sending off the sale papers.
suspects.motive: to find the letter that promises the cottage to the town before it ruins his sale

suspects.name: Beatrice Hollis
suspects.bio: Mrs. Pemberton's friend for fifty years. Keeps a lot of secrets, and keeps them well.
suspects.alibi: Says she was in the Living Room keeping Mrs. Pemberton company.
suspects.motive: because half the letters were written by her, and she'd rather nobody ever knew

clues.name: Leaf mould
clues.description: Damp black leaf mould trodden into the Study rug.

clues.name: Bookshop bag
clues.description: A crumpled paper bag from the Bookshop on Main Street.

clues.name: Sealing wax
clues.description: A chip of red sealing wax, the kind used on official papers.

clues.name: Rosewater
clues.description: The desk drawer smells of old-fashioned rosewater.

clues.name: Shed key
clues.description: The little brass key to the garden shed, left in the desk.

clues.name: Garden twine
clues.description: A length of green garden twine, like the bundle was tied with.

clues.name: Postage stamps
clues.description: A strip of new stamps, torn off in a hurry.

clues.name: Fountain pen ink
clues.description: Blue-black ink on the blotter, still wet.

cases.name: The Stolen Seed Corn
cases.premise: The Hatchers' prize seed corn, saved from every harvest for a hundred years, has been stolen from the Barn, and the scarecrow in the maze now turns its head to watch whoever walks by.
cases.recovered: The seed corn is back in the Barn, and next year's harvest is safe.

suspects.name: Abel Hatcher
suspects.bio: Worried about money since the prize display. Works later every night.
suspects.alibi: Says he was stacking bales in the Hayloft.
suspects.motive: to sell the seed corn quietly and pay off the debts he hasn't told his family about

suspects.name: Clementine Hatcher
suspects.bio: Keeps her crown on even to feed the chickens. Wants a farm of her own one day.
suspects.alibi: Claims she was in the Sewing Room finishing her parade cape.
suspects.motive: to plant it on her own patch and win next year's ribbon all by herself

suspects.name: Silas Crane
suspects.bio: Still trying to buy the farm. Brought a new offer, and new shoes.
suspects.alibi: Insists he was at the Hardware store in town buying fence wire.
suspects.motive: to ruin next year's harvest so the farm would have to sell to him

suspects.name: Ma Jessup
suspects.bio: Bakes for half the county and buys her cornmeal from nobody but the Hatchers.
suspects.alibi: Says she was at the Diner dropping off muffins.
suspects.motive: because only cornmeal from the old seed corn makes her prize muffins rise

clues.description: A paper napkin from the Diner with sums scribbled on it.

cases.name: The Silver Christening Cup
cases.premise: The Ashcombe christening cup, solid silver and two hundred years old, is gone from the Nursery, and every night since, the empty cradle has rocked by itself.
cases.recovered: The christening cup is back in the Nursery, and the cradle has finally stopped rocking.

suspects.name: Ezra Cole
suspects.bio: Looks after the house and the Family Plot. Says the old stones are crumbling.
suspects.alibi: Says he was in the Gazebo stringing up lanterns.
suspects.motive: to pawn it and pay for new headstones in the Family Plot, since nobody else would

suspects.name: Lavinia Ashcombe
suspects.bio: Has started labelling the family silver with her initials, 'just in case'.
suspects.alibi: Claims she was in the Tower Study writing letters.
suspects.motive: to have it engraved with her own name before the family could argue over it

suspects.name: Dr. Felix Marlowe
suspects.bio: Came back for the music box, stayed for the silver.
suspects.alibi: Insists he was at the Library in town reading about silver marks.
suspects.motive: to add it to his collection, where it belongs, in his opinion

suspects.name: Agnes Pratt
suspects.bio: Has polished the Ashcombe silver every Sunday for thirty years.
suspects.alibi: Says she was in the Kitchen polishing the rest of the silver.
suspects.motive: to hide the dent she put in it while polishing, before anyone noticed

clues.name: Lantern soot
clues.description: Black soot smudged on the cradle's rail.

clues.name: Lilac powder
clues.description: A dusting of lilac face powder on the windowsill.

cases.name: The Vanishing Portrait
cases.premise: Lady Blackwood's portrait has vanished from the Portrait Gallery, leaving a pale square on the wallpaper, and the old organ in the Cellar plays by itself at midnight.
cases.recovered: Lady Blackwood's portrait is back in the Portrait Gallery, and the organ in the Cellar is quiet at last.

suspects.name: Gus Thornbury
suspects.bio: Forty years on the grounds and, he says, ten years of wages owed.
suspects.alibi: Says he was raking leaves in the Cemetery.
suspects.motive: to get at the wall safe behind it, where he swears his unpaid wages are kept

suspects.name: Vivian Blackwood
suspects.bio: Owns the manor now. Owns slightly less of what's in it than she used to.
suspects.alibi: Claims she was in the Master Bedroom with a headache.
suspects.motive: to hide that the portrait shows the pearl necklace she has already sold

suspects.name: Reginald Pike
suspects.bio: Has a buyer in the city who wants 'anything old and Blackwood'.
suspects.alibi: Insists he was at the Barber in town having a shave.
suspects.motive: to sell the painting to his buyer in the city, frame and all

suspects.name: Martha Bunce
suspects.bio: Has been looking for Lady Blackwood's lost recipe book her whole life.
suspects.alibi: Says she was in the Cellar fetching jars of preserves.
suspects.motive: to find the recipe book Lady Blackwood hid behind the frame years ago

clues.description: Wet autumn leaves on the gallery floor.

clues.description: A smudge of pale face powder on the empty wall.

clues.description: A cut length of new picture wire.

clues.description: The Portrait Gallery key, left in the lock.

houses.name: Pemberton Cottage
houses.blurb: A tidy little cottage with a white picket fence. Mrs. Pemberton swears her teapot rattles at midnight. Small and quick: one floor, a garden and a shed.

houses.name: Hollow Creek Farm
houses.blurb: The Hatchers' farm at the edge of town. Lanterns float through the corn maze and something lives in the hayloft. Medium: a two-storey farmhouse, a barn and a big maze.

houses.name: Willow Lane Victorian
houses.blurb: The Ashcombe house: turrets, gingerbread trim and a music box that plays by itself in the nursery. Large: two floors and a tower, a gazebo and a family plot.

houses.name: Historical Society
houses.blurb: The Hollow Creek Historical Society: a red-brick museum with white columns, a gallery of folklore masks, a reading room that smells of lavender and old paper, and an archive upstairs. It may close after Halloween. Large: two floors, a courtyard and a workshop.

houses.name: Blackwood Manor
houses.blurb: The old Blackwood estate past the creek: a cellar, two floors and a roof, a greenhouse, a cemetery and a pumpkin patch. Huge: the longest night.

legends.name: The Headless Horseman
legends.legend: A Hessian trooper who lost his head to a cannonball. He rides at night looking for it, and throws a flaming jack-o'-lantern in its place.
legends.powerBlurb: hurl a flaming jack-o'-lantern that bursts in a ring of fear

legends.name: The Banshee
legends.legend: A pale spirit whose wail foretells a death in the family. Hearing it means trouble.
legends.powerBlurb: a scream heard through walls: big fear, flashlights knocked out

legends.name: Stingy Jack
legends.origin: Irish folk tale, the first jack-o'-lantern
legends.legend: He tricked the Devil twice, so neither Heaven nor Hell would have him. He wanders with a coal in a carved turnip: the will-o'-the-wisp.
legends.powerBlurb: three wisps drift out and hunt Solvers; a flashlight pops them

legends.name: Baba Yaga
legends.legend: The bony-legged witch of the deep woods. She flies in a mortar, steers with a pestle and curses anyone who wanders too close to her hut.
legends.powerBlurb: curse the nearest Solver: fear spikes and their flashlight drains
